title: Design a document ingestion system processing 100,000 updates/day
summary: Design a durable ingestion pipeline that survives duplicates, out-of-order updates, poison documents and provider throttling.
scenario: HarborDesk synchronizes support manuals from 80 upstream connectors. Upstreams provide at-least-once webhooks, periodic inventory snapshots and deletion events. A source may resend an old revision after a new one. The previous pipeline lost deletes during retries and left duplicate chunks in search. Design a replacement that can prove the visible index corresponds to the accepted source revision, recover after a long outage and replay safely. All scale figures are exercise assumptions.
requirements: Accept updates and deletes durably before acknowledging them; preserve source event ID, tenant, document ID and a comparable source revision.
Parse, normalize, chunk, embed and publish a complete document revision. Queries must not see a half-published mix of old and new chunks.
Handle duplicate deliveries, out-of-order events and worker crashes without duplicate visible chunks or resurrecting deleted documents.
Bound retries and quarantine permanent failures in a dead-letter workflow with enough diagnostics for safe operator replay.
Expose per-tenant lag, oldest pending event, stage latency, failure reasons, backlog and accepted-versus-indexed revision. Support controlled backfills.
scale: 100,000 document mutations/day; 85% updates and 15% deletes. Calculate average events/s and provision for a 30-times burst for 20 minutes.
Mean source payload 300 KB; p99 is 20 MB. Updates produce 50 chunks on average. Embedding endpoint quota is 1,200 chunks/s shared across tenants.
Parsing costs a mean 1.5 CPU-seconds/update. Embedding request latency averages 500 ms for a batch of 50 chunks; retry traffic consumes quota too.
Freshness objective: 95% of accepted changes searchable within 10 minutes under normal load. Recover a six-hour outage backlog within two hours while live traffic continues.
constraints: Upstream delivery is at-least-once. A globally ordered event stream is unavailable. Exactly-once claims must identify their actual transactional boundary.
Malformed or oversized documents must not block unrelated tenants. Enforce resource limits on parsing and staging.
The queue and index cannot share one database transaction. Explain outbox, checkpoint or reconciliation choices.
Deletion tombstones must survive the longest supported replay window, assumed here to be 30 days. Explain what happens beyond it.

prompts.diagram: Draw event acceptance, durable queue, parsing/chunking/embedding workers, staging, publication, tombstones, dead-letter handling and reconciliation. Label durable versus ephemeral state.
prompts.flow: Walk through update revision 12, duplicate revision 12, late revision 11 and delete revision 13. Identify idempotency keys, compare-and-set checks, acknowledgement timing and atomic visibility.
prompts.capacity: Calculate average and burst rates, embedding demand and CPU workers. Size six-hour backlog recovery alongside live traffic and compare it to quota. Include storage, headroom and a backpressure policy.
prompts.failures: Describe a worker crash before and after index publication, repeated embedding 429s, a poison PDF and a delayed delete. Give recovery, diagnostics, bounded retries and an invariant to test for each.
prompts.adr: Choose queue partitioning and publication strategy. Compare in-place writes with staged revision swaps or an equivalent design. Defend ordering, replay cost, dead-letter policy and the reconciliation schedule.

rubric.title: Acceptance and durability
rubric.question: Can every acknowledged mutation be recovered?
rubric.evidence: Name the durable acceptance boundary, ownership transfer and queue acknowledgement points.

rubric.title: Idempotency and revisions
rubric.question: Can retries or old events resurrect stale content?
rubric.evidence: Trace event identity, document revision compare-and-set, tombstones and replay-window limits.

rubric.title: Atomic search visibility
rubric.question: Can queries observe half of a document revision?
rubric.evidence: Show staging, publication pointer and safe garbage collection of old chunks.

rubric.title: Quota-aware recovery
rubric.question: Will your outage-recovery plan fit available throughput?
rubric.evidence: Compute update chunk demand, CPU budget and backlog drain while live traffic continues.

rubric.title: Recoverable failures
rubric.question: Can an operator safely replay a dead-letter item?
rubric.evidence: Document classification, retry bounds, replay validation, tenant fairness and lag alerts.

rubric.title: Consistency trade-offs
rubric.question: What guarantee holds across queue and index?
rubric.evidence: State transaction boundaries and defend reconciliation against a concrete failure sequence.

follow_ups: A connector has no monotonic source revision. What weaker guarantee can you support?
The embedding quota is halved for two hours. Which work is deferred and why?
A parser fix requires reprocessing all documents without replacing newer source edits. Design the backfill.
